summary: Customer reports receiving onboarding emails after unsubscribing (suppression rule not applied)
description:
Issue summary
A HelixSupport user reports receiving Redwood Inference onboarding emails after clicking the unsubscribe link (opt-out) in a previous message.

Why this matters (compliance)
Opt-out requests must be honored across marketing communications. This is compliance-sensitive (CAN-SPAM / GDPR). Treat as P1 until we can confirm suppression is correctly enforced and no additional emails will be sent.

Customer impact
- Customer received at least one additional lifecycle email after unsubscribing.
- Risk of reputational damage and compliance exposure if suppression is not reliably enforced for the onboarding series.

Customer report (from Support inbox → Jira)
- Customer email: support@helixsupport.ai (reported by: end user on their team)
- They clicked the unsubscribe link on 2025-01-23 ~18:10 PT.
- They received another email on 2025-01-24 ~09:02 PT.
- Email subject received after opt-out: "Get to first success in 5 minutes" (onboarding series)
- Customer request: confirm that they have been removed from all marketing emails and explain what happened.

Initial triage checklist
- Confirm unsubscribe event captured (provider + internal).
- Confirm suppression applied to all lifecycle campaigns (including “first-success” and “troubleshooting”).
- Ensure no further sends to the address while investigating.
- Determine if this was: (a) suppression propagation delay, (b) misclassified as operational/transactional, (c) segment/audience logic bug, or (d) duplicate profile / alias issue.

Investigation notes (internal)
1) Provider events
- Send event logs show the follow-up message was queued ~08:59 PT and accepted by ESP ~09:00 PT.
- Unsubscribe click event recorded ~18:10 PT the prior day.

2) Redwood lifecycle system behavior
- The onboarding series is triggered off “signup_completed” and “api_key_created/first_request_success” state transitions.
- Suppression is expected to be checked at send-time via the global opt-out flag in the marketing profile store.

3) Finding: suppression not applied for one workflow path
- We found that the onboarding workflow step “welcome_v1_first_success_nudge” was incorrectly configured to use an “operational” channel classification (intended for account/security notices).
- That path bypassed the global marketing opt-out/suppression list in our ESP integration.
- The affected email appears to be part of the lifecycle experiments sprint v1 sequence.

4) Scope assessment
- This is not isolated to HelixSupport; any user who unsubscribed but was still eligible for the misclassified step could receive additional emails.
- We did not see evidence of repeats beyond a single additional message, but we need to confirm by querying last 7 days sends where opt_out=true at send time.

Immediate mitigation
- Paused the specific workflow step “welcome_v1_first_success_nudge” while we verify suppression is enforced.
- Added HelixSupport domain and the reporting address to a temporary manual suppression list as a belt-and-suspenders measure.

Customer comms plan (compliance-sensitive)
- Do not email the customer again unless explicitly requested (to avoid further marketing contact).
- Provide confirmation via the existing support thread/portal response that they are suppressed from all marketing campaigns.
- Offer a short apology and state we fixed the workflow configuration.

Resolution
- Marketing Ops updated the workflow classification to marketing and confirmed the global suppression check is executed for the onboarding series.
- Ran a backfill job to re-sync opt-out flags to the ESP suppression list (to reduce any lingering propagation edge cases).
- Verified with a test profile: unsubscribe → attempt to trigger onboarding step → send blocked.

Follow-ups / action items
- Add an automated validation: any lifecycle email workflow must fail CI/checks if channel classification == operational.
- Add a daily monitor/alert: count of sends where opt_out=true at send time (should be 0).
- Post incident note to #support and #marketing with guidance and a one-liner explanation for frontline teams.

Notes
- Keep all customer identifiers in comments minimal; do not paste full email headers publicly. If needed, store raw headers in the restricted internal support folder and reference location only.
